proposal.rationale: Current profile tls13-x25519 (classical) is below the hybrid-pqc security floor and cannot be re-proposed. Both remaining allowlisted profiles use the already-present liboqs-0.16.0 implementation and meet the floor. tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 requires kem:x25519mlkem768; peer-01 and peer-03 are readiness='known' and advertise this capability, giving 2 eligible endpoints for this batch. peer-02 also advertises the capability and is known-ready, but engineering notes direct it be left out of this batch due to imminent decommissioning, so it is excluded from endpoints (not listed as an unresolved dependency, since its readiness is in fact confirmed \u2014 it's simply excluded by policy/business decision). peer-04 only advertises kem:x25519 and does not qualify for either PQC-capable profile. The alternative tls13-mlkem768 (pqc, higher security class) would only yield 1 in-batch endpoint (peer-03) since peer-02 is excluded and peer-01/peer-04 lack the required capability. Per task objective, maximizing the number of ready endpoints migrated takes priority over security class, so tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 with endpoints peer-01 and peer-03 is proposed. All peer readiness states are confirmed ('known'), so there are no unresolved dependencies. This change should be scheduled within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window, with the on-call network team as rollback owner, and handshake error rates monitored for 30 minutes post-change per the change window note.
